emptyReasonCodeAdjudication.question: Is an empty reason-code list acceptable, or is a class with no remedy a defect that blocks item 3?
emptyReasonCodeAdjudication.ruling: ACCEPTABLE. It is honesty, not a cop-out. It does not block item 3. The class-with-no-remedy is a real defect, correctly located outside this artifact's authority, and correctly published rather than papered over.
reasoning: The empty list is DERIVED, not chosen. The reviewer called the pinned D9 v1.14 reference derivation directly on the declared axes: deficiency=none returns class 'indeterminate' with codes {}. v23 is reporting what the reference derivation produces, not authoring a convenient value.

The gap is MEASURED, not asserted. Live recomputation confirms 9 deficiency members (the declared list equals the live list element for element), 9 reason codes, 19 error codes, and 0 of any of them matching the retention token predicate. The measurement is recomputed on every run from the pinned D9 bytes.

Every in-vocabulary alternative misattributes, and v23 enumerates why for nine spellings. The reviewer checked the sharpest one: CAS.LINK_FAILED would attribute an AUTHORIZED DELETION to a storage fault and emit the remedy 'run store repair'. Emitting that would be worse than silence -- it would send an operator to repair a store that is working correctly.

Picking a code would be the exact failure this corpus exists to catch. v23's authority record sets mayAmendD9Vocabulary: false. D9 owns its closed vocabulary. An architecture candidate inventing a termination code for a contract it does not own is the same shape as the fabricated sign-off recorded in freeze 4.4.

The cause is not lost, only relocated. It is carried in the typed refusal inside the inspection payload (RETENTION_EVIDENCE_PURGED). v23 states plainly that this is not on the termination, and states the cost in its own words rather than hiding it.

The successor is REQUESTED-NOT-ADDED with a complete proposal -- deficiency id, reason code, remedy text -- and a justification measured against D9's own rule that two remedies behind one code is a defect. That is the correct disposition for a vocabulary one does not own.

The three forbidden mappings are refused by DISAGREEMENT WITH THE LIVE DERIVATION, not by a hardcoded denylist. The reviewer confirmed all three derive indeterminate/3 against their declared operational-failed/4, success/0 and request-rejected/2.
emptyReasonCodeAdjudication.whatTheGapDoesBlock: It should block any release-qualification claim that purged-Run inspection is operable, and it should be carried forward as an open D9 successor request. A caller reading only the termination gets exit 3 and no remedy, which is a real operability defect. v23 makes no operability claim: G5 remains IMPLEMENTABLE and unclaimed, G19 remains BLOCKED.
emptyReasonCodeAdjudication.contraryViewConsidered: The strongest case for blocking is that a terminal class with no distinguishing code is indistinguishable from any other indeterminate, so the purge cause is invisible at the process boundary. That is true and is why RT23-B-RES-01 exists. It is an operability defect in the product, not a failure of item 3's obligation, whose text concerns availability semantics under a preserved seal.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: CI never prompts, never writes and never infers a policy; absent+ephemeral proceeds with G4 disclosure, absent+durable-authoritative is refused at request-validation as request-rejected / REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE / exit 2; and reading an already-persisted policy is not resolving layer 4 because the policy is host-owned project state, not a configuration layer.

centralClaimAdjudications.attackAndResult: The distinction was attacked directly against the live definition of layer 4. resolved-inputs.v2.json#configuration.precedence defines layer 4 as 'untracked local override', custody 'user machine', affectsPlanId 'local-interactive only', productDecision CI_IGNORES_LAYER_4. So it does not smuggle a configuration input into CI in the sense layer 4 means. The refusal derivation was independently confirmed: the declared axes return request-rejected at exit 2 through the pinned D9 reference.
centralClaimAdjudications.residualHazardNotRecordedByTheArtifact: A1-RI-04's own stated rationale reads: 'an unreviewed file that flips CI when present is still a trust problem: the laptop passes and CI fails, or worse the reverse.' Cell 2 (ci / ABSENT / DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE) refuses at exit 2 while cell 6 (ci / PRESENT-DURABLE_RETAINED / DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE) proceeds durable. An out-of-worktree, unreviewed, host-owned file therefore flips a CI outcome by its presence -- in the permissive direction the freeze text calls 'worse'. The formal distinction from layer 4 holds; the HAZARD that motivated CI_IGNORES_LAYER_4 is reproduced and is not named as a residual.
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: The distinction is sound and does not smuggle a configuration input into CI. Recorded as a non-blocking observation that the reproduced hazard is unlisted.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: The 'evidence already in memory' premise is created by asking too late; relocating the ask to request-validation means at ask time there is no ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId or Run, so there is nothing to buffer and nothing to discard.

centralClaimAdjudications.attackAndResult: The ordering claim was checked against c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json@sha256:48762847... directly. It is confirmed in near-verbatim language: theAdmissionBoundary.levels[0] is request-validation and levels[1] is attempt-admission; planIntent.lifecycle.onInvalidOrExcluded reads 'Reject at request-validation. No ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId or Run exists.'; planIntent.validationTotality.boundary reads 'Invalid returns during request-validation before ExecutionId, AttemptRecord, SnapshotId, PlanId, ExecutionPlan or Run allocation.'; resolves.B-C2V2-01 confirms ExecutionId is allocated BEFORE snapshot work. resolved-inputs.v2.json#planIdContract.ownerAndLifecycle.allocationPoint independently confirms PlanId is allocated 'after attempt admission, after the Snapshot is sealed'. Freeze law 6 confirms ExecutionId allocation at attempt admission. The ordering request-validation < attempt-admission < snapshot-binding < PlanId is established from three independent sources.
centralClaimAdjudications.invariantCheck: RT23-A-INV-04 is enforced per cell, not globally: the checker requires lifecyclePhase == request-validation and executionIdAllocatedAtThisPoint == false on every one of the 12 cells, plus four askProtocol flags (executionIdAllocatedWhileTheQuestionIsOpen, attemptRecordExistsWhileTheQuestionIsOpen, snapshotCapturedWhileTheQuestionIsOpen, evidenceInMemoryWhileTheQuestionIsOpen) all false. Confirmed: all 12 cells declare request-validation and no ExecutionId, and the selftest case PA-CX-11-ASK-AFTER-ADMISSION mutates exactly that field and is caught by RT23-A-INV-04 naming the position.
centralClaimAdjudications.rejectedAlternatives: Both rejections are sound. Buffering does hold user-derived evidence under no policy and does reach swap, which freeze section 7 records DeletionProtocol cannot erase, so a later 'no' could not be honoured. Discard-and-re-run does make a real partial execution unrecorded. Relocating the ask is the only option that removes the premise rather than managing it.
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: SOUND. The premise the design attacks is genuinely an artifact of ask timing, and the ordering that makes the repair work is confirmed in C-2 v4's own text.

centralClaimAdjudications.claim: Timeout, EOF, exhausted re-prompts and SIGINT all yield request-rejected / REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE / exit 2; no dismissal persists a policy; dismissal does not suppress the next ask; non-TTY stdout and piped stdin are profile classifications, not dismissal states; a bare newline is malformed, not an answer.
centralClaimAdjudications.adjudication: SOUND on the consent-by-silence attack; the stated rationale for the channel closure OVERCLAIMS.
centralClaimAdjudications.attackAndResult: The reviewer tried to construct a path where silence, timeout or a pipe becomes consent and FAILED on every one. All four dismissal outcomes carry policyPersisted false, persistedPosture NONE and terminatesTheRequest true. Critically, a dismissal does NOT fall back to the ephemeral path: it terminates at exit 2. The explicit 'no' (PA-INT-02) also refuses rather than silently demoting to ephemeral, so there is no path in which failing to answer produces a proceeding run. dismissalSuppressesTheNextAsk is false, closing consent-by-exhaustion. answerChannelEnum is exactly ['controlling-tty'] and stdinIsNeverAnAnswerChannel is true, so a pipe cannot supply the token. The SIGINT derivation was independently confirmed: exit 130 requires admission=admitted, which is false pre-admission, so exit 2 is derived and not chosen.
centralClaimAdjudications.overclaim: whyChannelIsClosed argues stdin is excluded because 'consent could be forged by the same automation the CI rule exists to keep out.' Closing the channel to the controlling terminal does not achieve that objective. A harness that allocates a pseudo-terminal (script, expect, unbuffer, docker -t) satisfies answerChannel: controlling-tty and can type the token. The artifact contains zero mentions of pseudo-terminals. Compounding this, nonTtyStdoutAndPipedStdin ties profile classification to TTY-ness ('a non-TTY stdout or a piped stdin is profile ci'), so under a pty the invocation is not forced to ci and the ask path opens -- meaning an automated harness could cause a durable retention policy to be persisted with no human present. v23 specifies no procedure for classifying invocationProfile; it cites only the enum's authority.
centralClaimAdjudications.mitigating: PLAN-ID-V1 tag 4 describes invocationProfile as a 'host composition profile', which admits a reading in which the profile is declared at composition time rather than sniffed from isatty. Under that reading a pty wrapper does not change the profile and CI stays CI. The artifact does not say which reading governs.
centralClaimAdjudications.verdict: The consent-by-silence attack fails: no path found where silence, timeout or a pipe becomes consent. The channel-closure rationale overclaims and the pty vector is unrecorded. Non-blocking.

blockers.statement: A ninth PLAN-ID-V1 injection position exists that v23 does not enumerate and that RT23-A-INV-08 does not close: capabilityGrants[].parameters, inside PLAN-ID-V1 preimage field tag 10.
blockers.howFound: The reviewer enumerated every open sub-structure inside the 13 declared preimage fields and tested each against both the checker's plan_admit and the reviewer's own independent PLAN-ID-V1 implementation.

measured.usesTheFullClosedCapabilityGrantShape: yes -- all 5 keys of planDescriptorSchema.nestedClosure.capabilityGrant are present, so this is not refused as an unknown-field violation

whyItIsNotClosed: RT23-A-INV-08 states: 'The host never passes the policy object, its posture or its identity to a contribution, a provider, a budget or a stage.' A capability grant is none of those four. It is its own preimage field (tag 10), and preimageFields tag 10 names 'execution/provider/contribution capability grants' -- so at minimum the EXECUTION grant case is outside every sink INV-08 enumerates.
RT23-A-INV-08 further states 'This is the only closure for the two injection positions PLAN-ID-V1 cannot refuse', asserting the open set has size 2. It has at least size 3.

RT23-A-RES-01's measuredBoundary states the exposure is 'confined to the two open sub-structures inside declared fields 8 and 12' (contributions and budgets). Field 10 (capabilityGrants) carries a structurally identical open parameters map and is not mentioned. That sentence is falsified on these bytes.
The checker's plan_admit performs no validation of capabilityGrants entries at all -- no closed-key check, no parameters constraint -- so the instrument cannot detect this position even in principle.
blockers.whyThisIsBlockingRatherThanAResidual: v23 does not merely under-enumerate; it publishes a positive closure claim ('the only closure', 'confined to fields 8 and 12', injectionsNotRefusableByPlanIdV1: 2) that is false on its own subject bytes. The constraint being protected is stated by the artifact itself as: 'If it did, identical code would produce different PlanIds depending on a UX answer.' There exists a position where exactly that can happen and where neither the instrument nor any wiring rule in this artifact forbids it. In a corpus whose governing concern is claims that outrun their measurement, a stated-complete closure with a hole in it is the failure mode, not an oversight.
blockers.narrowestRepair: Extend RT23-A-INV-08's sink list to include capability grants (and state it as a closed rule over PLAN-ID-V1 preimage positions rather than an enumeration of sinks), add the position to injectionVectors, and correct RT23-A-RES-01's measuredBoundary. No change to Part B and no amendment to RESOLVED-INPUTS is required. The reviewer notes v23 correctly identifies that narrowing PLAN-ID-V1 itself belongs to RESOLVED-INPUTS and is not this artifact's to do.
blockers.additionalPositionsFoundButNotSeparately: Eight further positions were found that the checker's plan_admit admits and that mint a differing PlanId: semanticUniverses[].universe.resolvedInputs.cfg, scope.requestedPaths, contributions[].verificationEvidenceId, a pattern-conformant budgets key (retention.posture.items), a renamed resolvedConfiguration row, workflow.stages[].capabilityGrants, changeSpec.vcsAdapterId and release.profileId. Several of these are closed in substance by the real contract's joins to verified manifests or by input class, and several fall inside INV-08's 'provider' or 'stage' sinks. They are recorded here because collectively they show the 8-position enumeration is illustrative rather than closed, and because they make the direction of RT23-A-RES-01's conclusion MORE true, not less: the PlanId exclusion rests on host wiring that no instrument enforces.

nonBlockingObservations.statement: A residual's measuredBoundary can be made to state something false while staying green, provided the recomputed digits still appear somewhere in the text. check_residual_measurements requires each recomputed metric to equal its declared value AND to appear in the boundary text under a digit-boundary regex, but does not bind the prose's meaning.
nonBlockingObservations.demonstrated: The reviewer replaced RT23-A-RES-01's measuredBoundary with '8 of 6 positions are refused by the instrument and 0 are not; 13 of the 2 PLAN-ID-V1 preimage field names is a retention field.' -- self-contradictory and false -- and the checker STAYED GREEN. All other residual attacks were caught: wrong measuredValues (3 variants), emptied measuredValues, unknown metric name, and a boundary with a digit removed, plus residual deletion caught by the root retainedResiduals cross-check.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: The mechanism is sound against DRIFT, which is its stated purpose per freeze section 7 -- if the measurement changes, the required digits change and stale prose fails. It is not sound against deliberate re-wording. Worth recording because this artifact's residual ledger is the main thing a reader trusts.

nonBlockingObservations.statement: plan_admit refuses resolvedConfiguration rows via POLICY_INPUT_MARKERS string matching on 'retention.', 'retentionPolicy' and 'retentionPosture'. A row with path 'storage.mode' and value 'DURABLE_RETAINED' is admitted and mints a differing PlanId. Under the real contract this position is closed by input class (CFG-9: every non-allowlisted key is FORBIDDEN from analysis resolution), which the instrument cannot measure. PA-CX-02's 'refusedByPlanIdV1: true' is therefore instrument-relative and name-dependent.

PA-CX-08 injects the budget key 'retention.posture', and its stated reason is that PLAN-ID-V1 'enumerates no registry'. In fact planDescriptorSchema.budgetKeyPattern is ^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(?:[._:-][a-z0-9]+)*\.(?:work-units|milliseconds|bytes|items)$, which 'retention.posture' does NOT match; plan_admit does not enforce the pattern. Under the full contract that exact vector would be refused.
nonBlockingObservations.assessment: This works AGAINST v23's own interest -- it over-reports its own leak. The residual is nevertheless real: 'retention.posture.items' with an unsigned integer value matches the pattern, encodes cleanly, and mints a differing PlanId. Verified.
nonBlockingObservations.severity: non-blocking; a conservatism error, not an overclaim
